identification: layout (mod 12) + assumption that the finest visible groups are the slide's finest

ctf_fit.model: 3 bars x PSF x camera pixel, plus uniform stray light; PSF Gaussian, or a Gaussian core + wider Gaussian halo when that fits clearly better

notes: Group number assumed (finest visible pair taken as the slide's finest). Pass --pixel-size (approx. is fine) or --coarsest-group to confirm; the alternative is 2 groups coarser.

Background matters here: raw image -> G5E5, after automatic black level 83 -> G7E2. The automatic estimate can't tell camera offset from stray light; take a dark frame (light blocked, same exposure) and pass --dark-frame for a corrected result.
Bars reach the camera's full scale (255) in 3 element(s) (G4E2-G4E4): clipped peaks bias contrast; lower the exposure if possible.
Skipped isolated failure G4E6 (C_H 18.1%, C_V 23.0%): the next element passes again, so it is treated as a local focus / field-of-view effect (--skip-isolated 0 to stop there).
Stopped at the first failing element G5E6 (C_H 19.3%, C_V 25.2%); finer elements up to G6E2 pass again (--limit-rule finest-pass would report G6E2).

The fitted CTF curve crosses 20% at 84.9 lp/mm, inside G6E3, while the element-by-element limit is G5E5. They can differ when elements near the threshold are within the measurement noise of it; the fit uses all elements at once.
CTF fit: the fitted contrast never rises far above the threshold, so where it crosses is poorly defined (see the uncertainty).
